reason: Start building rocky planetesimals by letting the stone and metal grains stick gently.
expectation: I expect a larger rocky aggregate, though further concentration will probably be needed before gravity takes over.

alternatives.reason: I considered starting with icy material, but chose the rocky route first.

effect: Rocky pebbles have formed, but simple sticking will eventually encounter bouncing and fragmentation.
reaction: The growth barrier makes the next stage more interesting.
reason: Apply gas drag to the rocky pebbles to follow their route toward a dense swarm.
expectation: I expect gas drag to change how the pebbles move through the disk, perhaps helping concentrate them.

alternatives.reason: I could start the icy route, but prefer to continue the rocky one first.

effect: Gas drag has put the rocky pebbles into drifting orbits, which can concentrate them in structured regions.
reaction: The connection between drag and concentration is useful.
reason: Use the pressure maximum to concentrate the drifting pebbles toward a dense swarm.
expectation: I expect the pebbles to gather near the pressure maximum, though gravity may still need to take over.

alternatives.reason: I could start the icy route, but want to follow the rocky pebbles further first.

effect: The pressure maximum concentrated the rocky solids into a dense swarm, offering a route past the sticking barrier.
reaction: It's satisfying to see concentration substitute for continual sticking.
reason: Apply gravity to the dense swarm to advance the rocky planetesimal goal.
expectation: I expect the swarm to collapse into rocky planetesimals.

alternatives.reason: I considered starting the icy route, but want to finish the rocky route first.

effect: Gravity collapsed the dense rocky swarm into planetesimals, completing the rocky goal; the icy goal remains.
reaction: The collapse provides a satisfying payoff to the concentration steps.
reason: Start the icy route with the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect gentle collisions to form icy aggregates or pebbles, which will need further concentration.

effect: Gentle collisions formed icy pebbles containing rock and volatile material; the icy planetesimal goal remains.
reaction: The icy route is following a familiar pattern so far.
reason: Apply gas drag to the icy pebbles, the only offered combination, to continue toward concentration.
expectation: I expect drifting icy pebbles, analogous to the rocky route.

effect: Gas drag concentrated the icy solids through collective feedback, unlike the rocky route’s pressure trap.
reaction: The different concentration mechanism is a useful surprise.
reason: Apply gravity to the concentrated swarm; this is the only offered combination and should advance the icy planetesimal goal.
expectation: I expect the swarm to collapse into icy planetesimals.

effect: Gravity bound the icy swarm into planetesimals, completing the remaining goal.
reaction: The icy bodies provide a clear payoff, with a useful caveat about water sources.

mostWorthwhile.text: Concentrating rocky pebbles at a pressure maximum was satisfying because it showed a way past the barrier to continued sticking.

leastWorthwhile.text: Starting the icy route felt repetitive at first because gentle collisions again produced pebbles.

surprise.text: Gas drag concentrated the icy swarm through collective feedback, rather than the pressure trap used for the rocky route.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though the offered compatible combinations made the sequence more guided than discovered.

continue.text: I would continue: the contrasting concentration mechanisms made me curious how these small bodies become worlds.
